Seminar Title:

Development of Light Weight Geopolymer Concrete using Fly Ash Cenosphere as a Replacement for Fine Aggregate

Abstract:

Geopolymer concrete (GPC) is an environmentally-friendly option to ordinary Portland Cement (OPC), given GPC&rsquos reduction in carbon emissions and superior material performance. This investigation analyzes lightweight geopolymer concrete (LWGC) made from fly ash cenospheres (FAC) as a partial fine aggregate replacement at percentage levels of (0%, 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, and 100%), using alkaline activator solutions of 12M and 14M. In order to prepare the geopolymer binder, fly ash, ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBS), sodium hydroxide (NaOH), and sodium silicate (Na₂SiO₃) were used. Experimental tests conducted to evaluate the various mixes included slump tests, compressive strength tests, split tensile strength tests, flexural strength tests, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and energy dispersive x-ray (EDX) analysis. Results obtained showed that all geopolymer mixes outperformed OPC concrete. However, workability was greater for the 12M mixes. C40FA60 provided the best performance among all mixes as it had the greatest compressive strength (47.8 MPa), tensile strength (3.65 MPa), and flexural strength (5.05 MPa) at 28 days for the 12M mix and the best compressive, tensile, and flexural strength (45 MPa, 3.53 MPa, and 4.85 MPa, respectively) for the 14M mix. SEM analysis demonstrated that there was a dense geopolymer matrix in all of the geopolymer samples. EDX analysis confirmed that the geopolymerization process was effective as indicated by the favorable Si/Al ratios. Based on the findings of this study, it can be concluded that cenosphere-based geopolymer concrete produces an environmentally-friendly, sustainable construction material with very lightweight and high-performance characteristics.
